title: Invocation Shield: lightweight compatibility validator for staged tool invocations
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a lightweight 'Invocation Shield' service that observes live canary and shadow traffic and validates structured outputs and function/tool invocation compatibility at deploy time and during rollouts. The shield will run a fast signature-and-semantic-diff against a pinned compatibility profile for the active model variant and emit pass/fail signals that can be used by the rollout orchestrator to trigger automatic rollback or pause. Goals: (1) detect breaking changes in function calls or structured output contracts within minutes, (2) keep overhead under 2% p95 latency increase for affected requests, (3) provide clear metrics and example diffs in Console for debugging.
acceptance_criteria: Invocation Shield runs in shadow and canary modes and produces compatibility verdicts for >99% of observed tool invocations
False positive rate for compatibility failures <1% on seeded non-breaking changes
End-to-end test with synthetic traffic demonstrates automatic rollback triggered on high-severity incompatibility within configured threshold (default: 0.5% failing invocations over 5 minutes)
Console shows example invocation diffs, top-3 mismatched arguments, and a signer for the expected schema payloads
Runtime overhead on p95 latency for canary requests is <2% when shield enabled
Integration tests exercising function-call name additions, argument reorderings, and new optional fields pass or are classified correctly according to tolerance settings

notes: Trade-offs discussed: strict schema enforcement reduces risk but increases false positives for wide-open function signatures; we will provide a 'tolerance' mode that uses heuristic matching and semantic similarity scoring
We will avoid full parser-level semantic checks for now to limit CPU usage; focus on stable features: function name, arg keys, argument primitive types, and top-level structured output shape
Considered using existing schema registry, but initial iteration will bundle expected compatibility profile with rollout config to keep runtime simple
Decision: shield runs as a separate stateless sidecar service ingesting a copy of the request/response stream (shadow) and emitting compact verdicts to kafka and rollout API

risks: Risk: noisy false positives on models that frequently change non-breaking outputs. Mitigation: default to tolerant mode for public hosted clusters and strict mode only for Dedicated/Private until tuned
Risk: latency impact under high QPS. Mitigation: sample 10% of traffic for full semantic checks and always run signature matching for 100% of canary traffic
Risk: PII leakage in debug diffs. Mitigation: integrate PII redactors and require redaction before diffs are stored or surfaced in Console
test_plan: Unit tests for signature extractor and diff engine (coverage >90%)
Integration tests: canary policy simulation with synthetic traffic and seeded incompatibilities
Load tests: verify p95 latency overhead <2% at target QPS for canary path
Chaos test: simulate partial service failure of shield sidecar and verify safe default (no automatic rollback)
